summary: EXCEPT returns distinct rows from the first SELECT that do not occur in the second SELECT.
documentation: EXCEPT returns distinct rows from the first SELECT that do not occur in the second SELECT. Both branches need compatible column counts. A final ORDER BY defines result display order.
returns: The distinct first-source rows absent from the second source.
caution: This is directional: reversing the two sources changes the result. Duplicate source rows are removed.
scenarios: Find inventory SKUs absent from a published catalog.
Compare expected attendee IDs against checked-in IDs.
Identify exported records missing from a second snapshot.
title: Find unpublished product codes
problem: Tables inventory(sku TEXT) and published(sku TEXT) contain non-NULL ASCII codes. Return distinct inventory codes absent from published as one sku column, ordered by SQLite binary text order. Matching is case-sensitive.
goal: Use EXCEPT or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Put inventory on the left of EXCEPT and published on the right.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query against the supplied tables.
SELECT 1;
